title: Basket weave baby blanket
subtitle: A textured 75 by 90 cm cot blanket in basket-weave stitch on 4 mm needles.
excerpt: A 75 by 90 cm cot blanket in DK basket weave stitch, a six-row repeat that alternates raised knit columns and purl columns in a grid. The finished surface resembles woven cloth. About 265 g of machine-washable DK.
sourceNotes: Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938), §Basket Weave, describes the stitch as a standard all-knit-and-purl texture pattern. Weldon's Practical Knitter, 5th series (1889), §Basket Stitch, gives a cot blanket in the same stitch at double-knitting weight.

knitting.gaugeText: 22 sts × 36 rows = 10 × 10 cm in basket weave stitch on 4 mm needles, unblocked.
knitting.gaugeInPatternStitch: 22 sts × 36 rows = 10 × 10 cm in basket weave (slightly longer per row than stocking stitch).

glossaryTerms.definition: A stitch pattern based on alternating blocks of stocking stitch and reverse stocking stitch. Over a six-stitch, six-row repeat, the blocks switch position every three rows, producing a surface that resembles woven cloth. Uses only knit and purl stitches.

content.text: A single-panel rectangle worked flat in
basket weave stitch
on 4 mm needles, finishing at 75 cm wide by 90 cm long.

Single-panel construction avoids seams. Basket weave was chosen over plain garter for its texture: the alternating blocks of knit and purl columns produce a raised grid that resembles woven cloth from a short distance. The stitch lies flat without blocking because knit and purl blocks balance across the fabric. Budget about 265 g (about 580 m / 635 yards) of machine-washable DK. Buy all the yarn at once in matched dye lots.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: 265 g (about 580 m / 635 yards) of DK-weight machine-washable yarn

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 4 mm (UK 8 / US 6) circular needle, 80 cm or longer

content.text: Gauge
22 stitches and 36 rows to 10 cm over basket weave stitch on 4 mm needles, unblocked. Swatch the full six-row pattern repeat for at least 15 cm before casting on.

If your gauge is 20 stitches per 10 cm with a 168-stitch cast-on, the blanket will come out about 84 cm wide. Row gauge matters for length: at 34 rows per 10 cm instead of 36, the same row count produces the blanket about 5 cm longer.
Stitches used
Pattern
Cast-on
Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 168 stitches (a multiple of 6 for the basket-weave repeat). Long-tail tail: (4 × 168) / 10 + 15 = 67.2 + 15 = 82 cm. Measure 95 cm.
Body (6-row repeat)
Rows 1 and 2 (RS odd, WS even): *k3, p3; repeat from * to end.
Row 3 (RS): *k3, p3; repeat from * to end.
Rows 4 and 5 (WS, RS): *p3, k3; repeat from * to end.
Row 6 (WS): *p3, k3; repeat from * to end.
Repeat rows 1 to 6 until the blanket measures 90 cm from the cast-on edge. When you set this aside, note which row of the six-row repeat you are on.
Stitch count check-ins
At row 162 (end of a repeat cycle, about 45 cm): count across. You should have 168 stitches (a multiple of 6). At row 323 (about 89.5 cm): count again before casting off.
Common faults

Block alignment shifting: one row in the six-row repeat was skipped or repeated, shifting the blocks by three stitches. The misalignment is visible as a diagonal line across the blanket. Count the rows within each repeat with a post-it note until the pattern is familiar.

Loose purl blocks: purl tension is naturally looser for many knitters. If the purl blocks look baggier than the knit blocks, work the purl stitches slightly tighter, or try a needle half a size smaller.
Cast-off
Cast off in pattern (k the knits, p the purls) on the last row of a complete repeat. Cast off with a relaxed tension.
Finishing
Weave in both ends on the wrong side, running each tail at least 5 cm along a row. The basket-weave pattern is reversible: either face can be the public side.
Care
Machine wash on a gentle 30-degree cycle if superwash DK. Lay flat to dry.
What to try next

From basket weave, a natural progression is a textured check pattern with a longer block repeat. The same technique and needle size apply; the six-row repeat is extended to eight or twelve rows for a bolder block.
